headline: All majors underwater on the 200-day; funding still positive but positioning tops out as whale moves diverge between assets.
paragraphs: The regime is bearish across the board. Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, XRP, BNB, Doge, and Cardano are all trading below their 200-day simple moving averages; none have established a golden cross. Bitcoin sits 49.1 percent below its 12-month high of $124,740, while Ethereum has fallen 61.4 percent from $4,818 and Cardano has collapsed 80.7 percent from $0.96. The entire major asset class remains in a confirmed downtrend by the standard technical measure.

Momentum shows fatigue but no outright reversal signal yet. Bitcoin's RSI-14 sits at 45.8 and Ethereum at 48.3, both neutral and neither overbought nor oversold. MACD tells a split story: Bitcoin and Ethereum have MACD below signal line, suggesting momentum weakness, while Solana, BNB, and Doge still have MACD above signal, meaning some upward pressure persists in those names despite price action. This divergence between momentum and trend is typical of a bounce within a downtrend, not a regime shift. Cardano's 30-day return of 27.81 percent and 7-day return of 6.8 percent stand out against its downstream peers, yet it remains both below the 200-day and with MACD above signal at RSI 54.5, a configuration that can sustain for weeks in corrective rallies.

Leverage positioning shows crowding in longs with funding still positive enough to incentivize holding the bet. Bitcoin's 8-hour funding sits at 0.01 percent, annualizing to 11.0 percent, while Ethereum's matches at 9.9 percent annualized. These levels are moderate but non-trivial, meaning longs are still paying shorts to hold exposure. The long-to-short ratio is stretched: Bitcoin 1.63 to 1, Ethereum 1.98 to 1, and extreme in Solana at 2.3 to 1 and Doge at 4.7 to 1. Open interest is substantial ($2.08 trillion in Bitcoin perpetuals, $1.36 trillion in Ethereum), so the leverage boat is full and tilted toward longs. Liquidations over the past 24 hours tell the asymmetry: Bitcoin saw $8.6 million in long liquidations versus $0.46 million in shorts, and Ethereum recorded $8.2 million longs versus $1.2 million shorts. Shorts are getting cleaned out faster than longs, a sign the long squeeze has room to run if price holds.

Whale activity over the past 24 hours shows outflow of $121.5 million net from exchanges, led by Bitcoin ($65.3 million off exchanges) and Ethereum ($56.2 million off exchanges). This pattern suggests accumulation at the margin, yet it sits alongside a confusing detail: the biggest moves onto exchanges include $66.5 million Bitcoin to Coinbase and $64.0 million Bitcoin to Binance, while the biggest moves off exchanges include $128.9 million Bitcoin from Kraken and $73.5 million from OKX. The net is outflow, but the volume is bidirectional. Over the recent weekly range, the past four weeks show outflow, inflow, inflow, then outflow again ($134 million off, $1.01 billion on, $1.10 billion on, $395 million off), suggesting a rotation rather than a decisive withdrawal. Stablecoin float totals $305.4 billion and has declined 1.37 percent over 30 days, meaning dry powder is slowly evaporating as the crowd either deploys it or leaves it off-exchange.

Fear and Greed stands at 29, labeled Fear, and sits near the low end of its 30-day range of 22 to 33. The crowd is cautious but not panicked. ETF flows into spot Bitcoin and Ethereum have turned negative on the day (August 10 saw outflows of $144.6 million Bitcoin and $14.6 million Ethereum), yet the five-session net is positive at $550.6 million and $241.0 million respectively, with only one day of negative direction recorded. Traditional finance is still accumulating into spot products on the week-to-date basis, even as today's print reversed. Total market cap declined 0.39 percent on the session; Bitcoin dominance holds steady at 56.4 percent.

Watch for a funding reset: if 8-hour funding on Bitcoin or Ethereum flips negative, it signals shorts have begun paying longs and the long crowding trade has become expensive relative to its risk. Monitor whether the 200-day breaches on any major (BTC, ETH), which would be the first structural signal of regime change. Track whether whale outflows persist over the coming week or reverse back onto exchanges, as the recent bidirectionality suggests indecision at the top of the market. Finally, observe whether liquidations continue to skew long-heavy; a shift to symmetric or short-favored liquidations would indicate the leverage imbalance has begun to unwind.
